page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.large is an arm64-based general-purpose instance powered by a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor on a KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is supported via ARM AES instructions. The configuration does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark data reflects moderate single-thread execution paired with throughput constraints typical of a dual-core boundary. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves an average single-core score of 1790.19 and a multi-core score of 3551.69. Geekbench tests register 1065.0 in single-core compute and 1945.0 in multi-core compute. Memory bandwidth testing shows uncached read speeds of 24.55 GB/sec and write speeds of 15.62 GB/sec. Application-oriented tests record static web serving throughput at 2.62 GB/sec and Redis SET performance at 2.69 million operations per second.

The primary architectural advantage of the ecs.g6r.large is its dedicated Ampere ARM cores, which eliminate simultaneous multithreading resource contention and ensure consistent execution. Tradeoffs include low total parallel throughput, lack of high-bandwidth vector extensions like AVX-512, and reliance on remote storage across a 1 Gbps network baseline. This configuration fits lightweight ARM software development, automated testing pipelines, entry-level microservices, low-traffic caching, and basic web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.large is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor and 8.0 GB of RAM. Operating without bundled local storage or GPU hardware, the instance relies on external block storage and delivers a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks reflect moderate single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-threaded scaling, marked by a stress-ng single-core score of 1790.19 and multi-core score of 3551.69. Uncached memory bandwidth yields 24.55 GB/sec for reads and 15.62 GB/sec for writes, while Redis achieves 2.69 million SET operations per second. The Ampere Altra architecture provides dedicated compute cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead, offering predictable operational efficiency for entry-level ARM environments. The configuration is primarily suited for ARM-native development, CI/CD testing, containerized microservices, light caching, and low-concurrency web serving.
